artifact.name: track-04-persistence-codec
artifact.title: CONFLICT-PROPERTY-PERSISTENCE-CODEC
artifact.scope: App::Property and PropertyList; the listed codec/serializer addresses; ClassSerializer; ISimulatorSerializable; cCellSerializableData; cGamePersistenceManager; save headers; envelopes; transactions; references; versions; migration; atomicity; nested serialization; and mode-transition persistence.
artifact.clean_room_rule: Ghidra output, SDK declarations, and historical research are evidence, not original source or runtime truth; no proprietary bytes or implementation are reproduced.

overall_conclusion: The minimum original persistence architecture is now statically bounded: a typed property codec, an attribute-driven object serializer with class/field identity and nested object references, a cSavedGameHeader wrapper, a database/stream coordinator, and an explicit mode-specific cCellSerializableData save candidate. The exact outer .spo/.prop envelope, all value payloads, object-pointer tables, migration policy, field survival, and complete failure atomicity remain unresolved.

adversarial_steps.name: authority and mutation firewall
adversarial_steps.question: Could imported names, decompiler output, or project state be mistaken for original behavior?
adversarial_steps.prediction: Direct binary access and call shape outrank SDK names; no Ghidra mutation or filesystem/runtime access is needed to answer the architecture question.
adversarial_steps.method: Queried only explicit program SporeApp.exe with read-only decompile, disassemble, xref, vtable, and structure operations; read historical artifacts and SDK declarations separately.
adversarial_steps.result: No mutation or runtime execution was performed. Static and semantic certainty are separated below.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The distinction between direct binary evidence and declaration-only evidence is the smallest authority separator; it was performed.

adversarial_steps.name: address and body disambiguation
adversarial_steps.question: Do the listed SDK/anchor addresses name the claimed methods?
adversarial_steps.prediction: If 0x00692880/0x006928C0 and 0x00693DD0/0x00693DE0 are aliases, the same containing body will be returned; actual Write/Read should show stream operations and attribute callbacks.
adversarial_steps.method: Compared get_function_by_address, callers, disassembly, and decompilation for both address pairs; traced 0x00692900, 0x00693E10, 0x00695B40, cSavedGameHeader wrappers, and cCell wrappers.
adversarial_steps.result: 0x00692880/0x006928C0 resolve to the same setup/constructor body; 0x00693DD0/0x00693DE0 resolve to the same teardown body. Actual attribute Write/Read are 0x00692900 and 0x00693E10.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The smallest separator is exact entry-point identity plus one stream/callback operation; it was performed and rejects the address-name conflation.

adversarial_steps.name: layout versus semantic attack
adversarial_steps.question: Does a field offset prove what the field means or survives a save?
adversarial_steps.prediction: A runtime offset can be certain while its label, persistence role, and wire meaning remain unknown; imported 4-byte Property metadata must not override direct +0x10/+0x12 accesses.
adversarial_steps.method: Compared direct Property getter/setter/copy code, PropertyList map stride, SDK declarations, and imported structure layouts.
adversarial_steps.result: The 20-byte inline Property representation is strongly confirmed as a runtime layout; exact type semantics and all payload encodings remain bounded. cGamePersistenceManager's 0x4c SDK view is demonstrably incomplete relative to direct this-relative accesses.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The smallest separator is a direct field access beyond the imported structure; it was performed at 0x006A3890, 0x00693390, 0x00B0C190, and 0x00B0C520.

adversarial_steps.name: writer/reader symmetry attack
adversarial_steps.question: Do the write and read paths have matching local framing and failure behavior?
adversarial_steps.prediction: A symmetric codec writes/reads the same type/flags/payload sequence; failure should short-circuit rather than silently continue.
adversarial_steps.method: Compared 0x006A1540 with 0x006A2F60, 0x00693390 with 0x00694440, 0x00692900 with 0x00693E10, and cCell methods at 0x00E51300/0x00E51370.
adversarial_steps.result: PropertyList count/ID/typed-value symmetry, Property type/flags symmetry, array count/size symmetry, and ClassSerializer class/attribute checks are supported. cSavedGameHeader uses matching ClassSerializer wrappers. Exact object envelope labels remain bounded.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The smallest separator is one matching field order observed on both sides; it was performed for all four codec pairs.

adversarial_steps.name: framing, envelope, and nesting attack
adversarial_steps.question: Is a structure itself the file record, or is it wrapped by a serializer envelope?
adversarial_steps.prediction: A cSavedGameHeader allocation of 0x68 and a cCellSerializableData allocation of 0xec should not be copied raw if their concrete methods construct ClassSerializer state and call attribute dispatchers.
adversarial_steps.method: Traced cSavedGameHeader vtable/factory at 0x00B274E0, wrappers at 0x00B26800/0x00B26840, cCell vtable construction at 0x00E61550, and nested serializer calls at 0x00E51300/0x00E51370.
adversarial_steps.result: Both are ISimulatorSerializable/ClassSerializer-backed objects, not proven raw fixed-size payloads. Nested serializable objects use class/attribute callbacks and identity tables; raw host pointers are not an allowed persistence representation.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The smallest separator is a concrete wrapper-to-ClassSerializer call; it was performed for both header and Cell state.

adversarial_steps.name: reference and identity attack
adversarial_steps.question: Are pointers, parent lists, object references, and class identities being conflated with host addresses?
adversarial_steps.prediction: PropertyList parent installation should use a manager lookup and three words rather than recursively copying parent pointers; ClassSerializer read should resolve stored IDs before callbacks; mode handoff should copy an in-memory object rather than serialize a pointer.
adversarial_steps.result: Property parent data is a three-word external reference branch with unresolved field order; ClassSerializer resolves class/attribute identity before callbacks; Cell handoff is an in-memory object replacement/copy. Exact ResourceKey wire order and pointer-table bytes remain unresolved.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The smallest separator is a manager/identity lookup versus a direct pointer write; it was performed at 0x006A2F60 and 0x00693E10.

adversarial_steps.name: version and migration attack
adversarial_steps.question: Are version fields, compatibility gates, and migration semantics being inferred from names alone?
adversarial_steps.prediction: The save path should materialize major/minor header values and the reader should consume them, but a complete migration matrix requires a concrete branch or runtime fixture.
adversarial_steps.method: Inspected cSavedGameHeader layout/vtable, save orchestration at 0x00B28EC0 and 0x00BB4BA0, serializer version interfaces, and historical version reports.
adversarial_steps.result: Header version carriers and a writer value consistent with major 3/minor 0x25 are supported. Version callbacks and class-object load/save surfaces exist, but no complete downgrade/upgrade/migration policy is proven.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The smallest separator is an actual version-bearing field/store or branch; it was performed for cSavedGameHeader and serializer version surfaces, not for an assumed migration matrix.

adversarial_steps.name: failure, atomicity, and recovery attack
adversarial_steps.question: Does a successful-looking path imply rollback, journaling, or crash atomicity?
adversarial_steps.prediction: Codec callbacks short-circuit on failure; file paths use temporary/backup replacement, but that is weaker than a single atomic transaction across all save artifacts.
adversarial_steps.method: Inspected Property/ClassSerializer false paths, 0x00693D60/0x00693CD0 stream setup, 0x00693900 teardown, 0x006891F0 replacement, and save writers 0x00B28EC0/0x00BB4BA0.
adversarial_steps.result: No codec rollback is present in the local read/write paths. Temp/.old/rename handling is directly visible for identified save artifacts; complete .spo transaction atomicity, crash recovery, and cross-file consistency are not proven.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The smallest separator is a post-close temp/backup replacement call; it was performed. It supports replacement, not universal crash atomicity.

adversarial_steps.name: architecture decision and runtime narrowing
adversarial_steps.question: Can the minimum OpenSpore persistence architecture be decided without another runtime run?
adversarial_steps.prediction: The codec, class envelope, stream lifecycle, header, and Cell handoff boundaries are already sufficient to choose interfaces; runtime is needed only for exact wire bytes, migration, and save/load ordering.
adversarial_steps.method: Synthesized direct static evidence, SDK declarations, historical boundaries, and the existing negative runtime record; no new runtime run was launched.
adversarial_steps.result: Architecture is decided at the minimum-semantics level. Runtime is required for atomicity/failure behavior, migration validation, and field-survival/round-trip evidence; it is not required merely to decide that the outer wire bytes remain open. Wire-byte closure is separated from runtime-dependent semantic closure below.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The smallest architecture separator is stream/header/serializer ownership versus live mode state; it was performed statically. Runtime was not narrowed further.

hypotheses.subject: Property runtime layout
hypotheses.claim: The runtime Property is an inline 0x14-byte value carrier with flags at +0x10 and type at +0x12; the imported 4-byte Ghidra structure is a narrow tail/metadata view.
predictions: A Property getter or setter must access the value before the +0x10/+0x12 tail.
A PropertyList map entry must have a 0x18-byte stride with a four-byte ID followed by the 0x14-byte Property.
A type/flags-aware wire codec must not use the 4-byte structure as the entry size.

evidence_for.observation: 0x00422EB0 accesses the tail metadata and copies the scalar into the value body before setting Int32 type/flags.
0x006A3890 reads type at +0x12 and tests flags at +0x10, including pointer/array flag behavior.
0x00693390 reads type at +0x12 and flags at +0x10 before dispatching payload.
0x006A1540 writes each 0x18-byte map element and passes element+4 to the typed Property writer.
SDK Property declares a 0x14-byte value-plus-flags/type layout.

evidence_against.observation: The imported Ghidra Property structure is 4 bytes with flags/type at +0/+2; this is retained as a conflicting representation, not silently discarded.
Not every type-specific payload and unknown type branch is directly decoded in this pass.

hypotheses.independence: Direct getter, setter, typed writer, and map-stride accesses are separate binary paths; SDK support is corroborating but not independent of the imported layout.
hypotheses.repetition: The same +0x10/+0x12 pattern recurs in setter, getter, writer, and reader; recurrence is direct control-flow evidence, not a runtime round trip.
hypotheses.separator_result: Direct +0x10/+0x12 accesses and 0x18 map stride reject the 4-byte entry model for runtime object layout.
hypotheses.architecture_dependency: Freeze the 0x14 runtime value carrier and 0x18 map element; defer full payload semantics.

hypotheses.subject: PropertyList stream framing
hypotheses.claim: PropertyList Read/Write use a signed 32-bit count followed by local uint32 property IDs and typed Property values; a negative count selects a three-word parent-reference branch before local entries are read.
predictions: Write must emit count before each ID/value pair.
Read must resize the local map from the absolute count and stop on the first ID or Property failure.
The negative branch must install a parent through a manager virtual rather than recursively copy the parent map.

evidence_for.observation: 0x006A1540 computes local count from the 0x18-stride map, writes count, then writes each ID and calls 0x00693390 at element+4.
0x006A2F60 reads one count, branches negative, reads three 32-bit words, calls the manager virtual at +0x2c, then resizes and reads entries.
The 32-bit writer 0x0093AA70 and reader 0x0093A780 byte-swap in the mode used by PropertyList; the separate 16-bit writer/reader pair is 0x0093A9D0/0x0093A700.

evidence_against.observation: The outer PROP record envelope and compression are not covered by these local methods.
The semantic order and use of all three parent words remain unresolved.

hypotheses.independence: Write and Read are independent direct bodies with matching local framing; the parent manager call is a separate identity-resolution path.
hypotheses.repetition: The count-first shape is repeated in both methods and in the typed entry loop; it is not inferred from the SDK comment.
hypotheses.separator_result: Direct count/ID/value and negative-parent control flow supports the bounded local framing claim; it does not close the outer envelope.
hypotheses.architecture_dependency: Persist local entries and references, not the parent pointer or operation counter.

hypotheses.subject: Property typed-value wire shape
hypotheses.claim: The typed Property wire payload begins with 16-bit type then 16-bit flags; array/pointer flags are followed by 32-bit element count and element size before typed elements, while the default branch uses a fixed 0x10-byte raw payload.
predictions: Writer and reader must use the same type/flags order.
Array/pointer flags must gate a count/size prefix and element loop.
The normal mode must byte-swap 16-bit and 32-bit integer words.

evidence_for.observation: 0x00693390 writes type at +0x12, then flags at +0x10, then branches on flags 0x30/0x40 and writes count/size before elements.
0x00694440 reads type then flags, allocates count*size storage, and dispatches each element.
0x0093A9D0/0x0093A700 are the 16-bit writer/reader pair; 0x0093AA70/0x0093A780 are the 32-bit writer/reader pair. Both byte-swap when mode 0 is used.
SDK SerializationTypes declares typed primitive and container codecs, consistent with the bounded branches.

evidence_against.observation: Unknown/default types, string edge cases, and all pointer/object semantics are not closed.
The 4-byte imported Property layout does not describe the wire payload safely.

hypotheses.independence: The writer, reader, and primitive helpers are separate direct bodies; SDK declarations corroborate types but do not prove original wire bytes.
hypotheses.repetition: Type/flags order recurs in both codec directions; count/size ordering is independently visible in writer and reader branches.
hypotheses.separator_result: The smallest separator is the type/flags read/write sequence plus array count/size branch; it was performed.
hypotheses.architecture_dependency: Freeze only the proven envelope and dispatch shape; keep unknown type payloads behind adapters.

hypotheses.subject: ClassSerializer address identity
hypotheses.claim: 0x00692880/0x006928C0 are the same ClassSerializer setup/constructor body, 0x00693DD0/0x00693DE0 are the same teardown body, and the actual attribute Write/Read bodies are 0x00692900 and 0x00693E10.
predictions: A setup body should initialize pObject, pAttributes, counts, class ID, and up to 128 attribute pointers.
A teardown body should release attribute storage and not read/write a stream.
A true Write/Read body should call stream primitives and attribute callbacks.

evidence_for.observation: Ghidra resolves both 0x00692880 and 0x006928C0 to FUN_00692880; the body initializes ClassSerializer fields and copies attribute metadata.
Ghidra resolves both 0x00693DD0 and 0x00693DE0 to FUN_00693DD0; the body releases two attribute arrays.
0x00692900 writes class/stream framing, invokes attribute write callbacks, records sizes, and finalizes through stream status.
0x00693E10 reads class/stream framing, validates class ID/count, resolves attribute IDs, invokes read callbacks, and returns false on mismatch/failure.

evidence_against.observation: SDK XML/legacy anchors label the interior addresses as Write/Read; those labels conflict with the direct body identity and are retained as historical alternatives.
The old decomp-gap ledger recorded calls at 0x00692F9F and 0x00693D033 but did not identify the correct containing bodies.

hypotheses.independence: Exact function-boundary queries, direct caller edges, and disassembly are independent of SDK labels.
hypotheses.repetition: The same alias resolution occurs independently for both address pairs; the actual writer/reader are then confirmed by stream/callback operations.
hypotheses.separator_result: The smallest separator is whether the body touches stream/attribute callbacks; setup/teardown do not, while 0x00692900/0x00693E10 do.
hypotheses.architecture_dependency: Use 0x00692900/0x00693E10 as the concrete ClassSerializer codec boundary; retain setup/teardown aliases as non-codec operations.

hypotheses.subject: ClassSerializer object envelope and nesting
hypotheses.claim: ClassSerializer uses a class ID and an attribute-descriptor pass before/around callback payloads; reads validate class identity and resolve attribute IDs before invoking callbacks, supporting nested serializable objects and object-reference indirection.
predictions: Write should reserve or emit descriptor metadata before callback payloads and record per-attribute sizes.
Read should reject a class ID mismatch and resolve each stored attribute ID through the descriptor table.
Nested objects should be handled by serializer callbacks or object identity helpers, not raw host pointer writes.

evidence_for.observation: 0x00692900 performs a first framing/metadata pass, invokes attribute write callbacks, records sizes, then emits descriptor-sized tables and final stream status.
0x00693E10 reads framing, compares the stored class ID with +0xA08, reads descriptor pairs, resolves IDs through 0x00E0E9F0, and invokes read callbacks.
0x00695B40 constructs a ClassSerializer, calls 0x00695770 to dispatch attributes, and uses object/list helpers for identity bookkeeping.
The SDK declares object-pointer operations, class-object load/save, and nested ISimulatorSerializable interfaces.

evidence_against.observation: The exact outer database/COM envelope, CRC bytes, pointer table encoding, and all class IDs are not directly recovered.
The prior synthesis explicitly retained the object-pointer table and wire order as unknown.

hypotheses.independence: Direct writer/reader bodies and the object-dispatch helper are separate paths; SDK interface declarations are supporting architecture evidence.
hypotheses.repetition: Class ID and attribute identity checks occur on both write metadata and read resolution paths; the same helper is reused for nested objects.
hypotheses.separator_result: The smallest separator is class-ID/attribute-ID resolution before callback invocation; it was performed.
hypotheses.architecture_dependency: Implement a class/attribute registry, nested object references, and deferred pointer tables; do not serialize host pointers.

hypotheses.subject: cSavedGameHeader representation
hypotheses.claim: cSavedGameHeader is a 0x68-byte ISimulatorSerializable wrapper whose concrete Write/Read methods use ClassSerializer, not a raw 0x68-byte file block.
predictions: A constructor/factory should allocate 0x68 and initialize a map/header state.
The concrete vtable should route Write/Read to 0x00692900/0x00693E10 through 0x00B26800/0x00B26840.
Header fields should be callback-serialized rather than copied as one struct.

evidence_for.observation: 0x00B274E0 allocates 0x68, installs cSavedGameHeader vtables, and initializes the object-count map.
0x00B26800 constructs ClassSerializer state and calls 0x00692900; 0x00B26840 constructs the same state and calls 0x00693E10.
The vtable includes the cSavedGameHeader name/type surface and the header object is referenced by SP_Simulator/cSavedGameHeader/COM.
SDK cSavedGameHeader declares major/minor version, object-count map, timestamp, mode, snapshot, and current planet key at the expected offsets.

evidence_against.observation: No raw header bytes or complete callback attribute table are available; exact field emission order is not proven.
The actual file placement of the header inside the outer .spo envelope remains unresolved.

hypotheses.independence: Direct allocation/vtable/call-chain evidence is independent of SDK field declarations; SDK confirms names and offsets only.
hypotheses.repetition: Write and Read wrappers independently call the two ClassSerializer bodies with the same header attribute descriptor.
hypotheses.separator_result: The smallest separator is the concrete header Write/Read wrapper's ClassSerializer call; it was performed.
hypotheses.architecture_dependency: Use a versioned header object and callback/schema registry, not a raw struct writer.

hypotheses.subject: cCellSerializableData ownership and mode handoff
hypotheses.claim: cCellSerializableData is a 0xec ISimulatorSerializable state object held at cCellGame+0x5190; mode-transition paths allocate/copy/re-adopt it in memory, which is a persistence candidate but not evidence of automatic disk save.
predictions: The constructor should allocate exactly 0xec and install serializable/refcount vtables.
Write/Read methods should call ClassSerializer with the Cell class descriptor and a class ID.
Mode handoff should copy fields and publish/adopt a pointer without an I/O stream call.

evidence_for.observation: 0x00E61550 allocates 0xec, installs cCellSerializableData vtables, initializes fields, missions, and flags.
0x00E51300/0x00E51370 contain concrete write/read sequences: a 32-bit stream word followed by ClassSerializer setup and 0x00692900/0x00693E10.
0x00E627A0 copies the serializable state fields and 0x00E63D10 replaces the global handoff object without a stream call.
0x00E80BA0 adopts the global serializable-data object at cCellGame+0x5190, marks the handoff, and clears the global slot.
The SDK declares cCellSerializableData as ISimulatorSerializable with progression, mission, key, counter, and flag fields.

evidence_against.observation: Historical research retained exact per-field write coverage, defaults, and cross-stage handoff as unknown.
No positive original-process save/load trace or captured .spo/.prop round trip exists.

hypotheses.independence: Constructor, concrete write/read disassembly, copy helper, and CellGame adoption are distinct direct paths; historical reports repeat but do not add independence.
hypotheses.repetition: The same 0xec allocation and +0x5190 ownership recur in constructor, initialization, and historical structure evidence; write/read methods independently establish codec eligibility.
hypotheses.separator_result: The smallest separator is an I/O stream call versus an in-memory pointer/copy path; it was performed. The handoff is transient transfer, not disk persistence.
hypotheses.architecture_dependency: Persist an explicit Cell state DTO through the object serializer; keep live pools, queries, GFX, UI, and display state transient.

hypotheses.subject: cGamePersistenceManager size and role
hypotheses.claim: cGamePersistenceManager::Get returns a runtime service pointer; 0x00B0C190 and 0x00B0C520 are this-relative service lifecycle/mode methods on a much larger object than the SDK 0x4c view, not standalone save codecs.
predictions: Callers should load the Get result into ECX before calling 0x00B0C190/0x00B0C520.
The methods should access fields beyond the SDK structure if the object is larger.
